newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel wants wider mandate for new Bosnia force.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel wants wider mandate for new Bosnia force.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said he wants the mandate for an envisaged follow-on force in Bosnia to be widened, giving NATO-led troops the authority to seek out alleged war criminals.

In an interview with Bild newspaper released ahead of Sunday's publication, Kinkel said he was making a new appeal to the former warring factions to stick to the promises they made in the Dayton peace agreement one year ago.

"IFOR's mandate permits no active search for war criminals. Whoever wants to change that, must widen the new mandate which has yet to be decided. I am personally in favour of the NATO mandate in this question being made harder," he said.
"Only in this way can we remain credible to the victims of war criminals, and only then will suspected war criminals, including Karadzic and Mladic, know what is in store for them."

The new international force is expected to total about 30,000 troops and would replace a current NATO-led peace implementation force of 50,000, known as IFOR, which is being withdrawn from Bosnia this year.

"The former warring parties are obliged to send war criminals to the International War Crimes Tribunal in The Hague," Kinkel told Bild. "They promised this in the Dayton peace treaty and I am making a new appeal to them to stick to the very letter of those promises."
Most of the 16 NATO nations have already informally approved the new force to replace IFOR. Germany's parliament will vote in December on whether to extend the mission of its troops in Bosnia.
Russia and a number of other non-NATO states are likely to continue to take part in the follow-on effort, which would also station about 3,000 German troops in Bosnia.
But Western powers differed publicly at a Paris conference on Thursday over the duration of an extended mandate for a NATO-led peace force.
Kinkel said Bonn wanted it limited to one year. It would be wrong to give the rival Bosnian factions the impression that international aid could be dragged out over several years, he said.
